overview: Black plays a rim pawn move that weakens the kingside and gives White a free hand to take the centre with d4 and Nf3. White simply develops and builds a big centre, and Black tries to answer with ...d5 or ...e5 and a later ...Nf6 or ...Bg4. It is a joke or surprise reply that relies on White taking it lightly.

white_ideas.idea: d4, Nf3 and Bd3, taking the centre while ignoring the h-pawn.
Push the e-pawn or attack the weakened kingside with Ng5 or Bd3 ideas.

black_ideas.idea: ...d5, ...Nf6 and ...Bg4, reaching a playable position with the h-pawn advanced.
...Rh6 or ...Nf6 with an odd rook lift.

typical_structures.structure: Ordinary centre with Black's h5 pawn weakening g5 and the kingside.

character.notes: No forcing line, just an odd move; low confidence.

soundness.notes: Dubious: gives White a free tempo and a weakened kingside, though no forced refutation.

approach.notes: Played by almost no strong players, for surprise.

level.notes: Easy to understand but a poor choice; dubious so not beginner.

character.reason: Neither a forcing nor a solid line; low confidence.

soundness.reason: Wastes a tempo and weakens the kingside.

structure.reason: Centre not yet decided, no clear structure.

level.reason: Dubious so never beginner; no theory to memorise.
